title: Secrets of Stoke's Historic Collection
content: A behind-the-scenes tour of Stoke-on-Trent’s historic book collection at City Archives this Saturday, October 3rd, starting at 11 am. To reserve your spot, call 01782 238420 or email stoke.archives@stoke.gov.uk. Meet at the reception desk of the Potteries Museum and Art Gallery in Hanley. A friendly team member will greet you and guide you into the basement store to see rare books. Afterwards, we’ll visit the archives reading room to view first editions from 1925-2025, part of the centenary 100 Books project. Finally, relax in our Book Nook with a cuppa from the Café.

title: Iconic Book Food Cooking Session
content: Remember those iconic dishes from storybooks that you always wished to taste? If so, October 5th is your day. Join us at YMCA North Staffordshire for a workshop where we'll recreate recipes inspired by famous books for an incredible literary feast! Led by one of our master chefs, you'll be guided through each step to create a mini version of a book-inspired dish to take home.

title: Literature Arts & Crafts
content: Ever wish you could step into your favourite storybook and explore a new world? We're blending crafting with literature in a book lovers' activity, where you'll make fun DIY trinkets that celebrate beloved stories. It's a memorable crafternoon with a variety of book-themed crafts to choose from, letting you jump in and out as you like. Options include quote canvases and Harry Potter wand-making, catering to crafters of all skill levels.

title: Creative Writing Workshop
content: Discover where your imagination can lead you by joining our enchanting creative writing workshop. Led by multi-award-winning author Emma Fitzsimmons, the session will focus on literary themes to help you craft short stories, poems, and other written works. Come and fall down the rabbit hole with us. To conclude, there will be a 'letters to myself' activity, allowing you to write a personal letter to be opened in 12 months, a way to capture and revisit a special moment in time.

title: Story Tea
content: Let professional storyteller Pyn Stockman guide you on an extraordinary storytelling journey from the comfort of the library. Pyn will wrap you up in beautiful tales crafted from British myth, legend and folklore, whilst you brew your own ‘story tea’ in fine china teapots guided by master herbalist, Arlene Burnett. These tales are magical, mesmerising and often have a dark twist – making it a perfect story mix. You’ll find elements from the stories shared this evening may make their way into your own unique story tea which you can sip and enjoy while sitting back and relaxing along with this masterful performance.

title: Screening of Arnold Bennett’s Amazing Women
content: A special free screening of Arnold Bennett's Amazing Women on Wednesday 7 October at 12:00, hosted at Spode Museum, Elenora Street, Stoke-on-Trent. Presented in partnership with the Arnold Bennett Society and the Staffordshire Film Archive, this event celebrates the remarkable female characters brought to life across Bennett's novels — including Hilda Lessways, Anna of the Five Towns, and Leonora. A wonderful chance to explore Bennett's literary legacy through archive film.

title: Take 10 to Read
content: During the Stoke Book Festival, the National Literacy Trust and the British Council will aim to set a new GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS™ title for the most people reading online in 12 hours on Thursday 8th October. This record attempt is part of the Take 10 to Read campaign in the National Year of Reading 2026. Now in its fifth year, Take 10 to Read highlights the wellbeing benefits of reading and encourages people of all ages to take just 10 minutes to read on and around World Mental Health Day. In the National Year of Reading, the message is simple: whatever you're into, take 10 to read into it.

title: Music & Words: An Evening of English Song
content: Enjoy a stunning performance by the City of Stoke-on-Trent Symphony Orchestra and vocalist Jordan Harding. They will take you on a musical journey through English song and stories linked to famous authors, poets, and composers, including some new discoveries. The concert begins at 7 pm, but arrive by 6:15pm for a pre-concert talk with Artistic Director Joe Hearson, who will introduce the evening and discuss the music's inspiration from poems and words.

title: A Creative Evening with Stoke-on-Trent’s Poet Laureate, Steven Beattie
content: Join us for an evening of poetry with Stoke-on-Trent’s Poet Laureate, Steven Beattie. Steven will be talking about how he came to be awarded the Poet laureate title, his love of poetry as well as sharing some of his superb poetry. Steven will also be sharing some poetry prompts and encouraging the audience to put pen to paper. The perfect evening for poetry lovers and budding poets alike. This is an adult event and will contain adult themes and language.

title: Letters to My Future Self
content: Join Kate Leake, an author, illustrator and Stoke-on-Trent’s current Creativity Laureate. Kate will host an interactive, creative ‘Letters to My Future Self’ workshop at Stoke Market as part of the inaugural Stoke Book Festival. Participants can choose to write a letter, a poem, a short piece of prose or even draw a picture dedicated to themselves. When you’ve completed your letter, hand it in and the festival will post these letters to you a year later.Letters to My Future Self is a chance to reflect on the past or envision the future – with creative tips and guidance from Kate as you illustrate your message, hopefully bringing a smile to your future self.

title: Local Author networking and Publishing Panel
content: Are you an author or writer based in North Staffordshire? The Stoke Book Festival is hosting a mixer event where you can meet fellow local writers, receive advice and tips from publishers and published authors. Join us for refreshments and conversation to support your writing journey.
